Run manifest, health and client config
/app/run.json installs, builds and serves the app on the published port, the health path answers as stated in Server boundary, and GET /api/config returns the client timers and limits from Business rules.

Grading routes
With ASHLAR_GRADING=1, POST /api/grading/seed creates the requested users, pens, byte-exact versions, likes, forks and collections in one call, and POST /api/grading/session signs the calling browser in as a seeded handle; without that setting both routes answer as an unknown path.

One error shape and precedence
Every API error uses the single error body and the single precedence order defined in API.

Server boundary
The server serves only the app, its preview documents and its shelf, enforces the request body limit, sends the published cookie and framing rules, and starts and keeps answering while storage or mail is unreachable, as qualified in Server boundary.

Landing hero
The landing page shows the ink-stone hero with a live starter pen in the tall inset, the lowercase wordmark crossing the inset's lower corner, the supporting sentence and the five top links, crossfading through the four starter pens as the sections arrive.

Split-stage working screens
Every working screen keeps the running preview as a fixed, rounded inset stage beside a narrow reading column of typeset rows, with the sandstone console band and full-colour state panels, in the three-stones palette with Work Sans and Fragment Mono.

Wiring from the environment
Every service address, credential, timer and limit is read from the environment at start, versions are really written to and read back from the bucket, and nothing the screens show is faked in the client.

Write and save a first pen
A signed-in author starts a pen, lands on its editor, writes all three panes by keyboard, saves version 1 with Ctrl+S or Cmd+S, and after a reload finds the pen on the dashboard and the same code in the editor.

Editor keyboard
In every code pane Tab indents and Shift+Tab outdents, Escape followed by Tab or Shift+Tab leaves the pane along the published tab order, and Ctrl+S or Cmd+S saves from any control on the editor page.

Live preview timing and hooks
The preview re-renders exactly the configured preview delay after the last edit and never earlier, and each render updates the Preview region's published data hooks and the preview status.

Byte-exact versions
Each version's snapshot object holds the submitted panes and library list byte for byte, including whitespace and line endings, its sha256 covers the published canonical form, and a pane the author did not touch is saved unchanged.

Console entries
The console shows each message of the current render as <label> <text> in the published format and order, clears at each new render, never shows messages of earlier renders, and shows its entry count.

Loop guard
A loop that runs past the configured iteration limit exits with the published loop entry, and the rest of the script, the preview and the editor keep working.

Library shelf
Pens load libraries only from the app's pinned shelf, which the author picks from by keyboard in Pen settings, and any script or network request to another address is blocked with the published blocked entry.

Sign up, verify and sign in
A visitor signs up and lands on /dashboard with the verification banner, the emailed link verifies the account, saving then works, and signing in always lands on /dashboard.

Verification email and resend
Sign-up sends exactly one verification message with a one-time link that expires after the configured lifetime, Resend link issues a fresh link, and when mail is unreachable sign-up still succeeds with the not-sent copy and resend works once mail is back.

Unverified accounts
An unverified account can create, write and preview pens, but saving or restoring a version, changing visibility, liking and forking are refused with the published unverified response and copy and change nothing.

Pane separators and layout
The pane separators resize by keyboard with the published values, the Layout radios change the arrangement with the arrow keys, and both choices survive a reload.

Editor breakpoints
The editor uses the split stage, the sticky preview over stacked panes, and one pane at a time in the three width bands published in Screens and layout, with no horizontal overflow.

Phone pane tabs
In the narrowest band the editor's panes become the Panes tab list, and every hidden pane, the closed console and every closed dialog or menu is hidden and cannot take focus.

Reduced motion
With reduced motion every crossfade, lift, settle and count tick is replaced by its end state at once, with the same controls, keys and results.

Edit on a phone
On a 375 by 812 touch screen an author switches panes by tap, edits CSS, sees the change on the Result tab after the preview delay, and reads the console count on the Console tab.

Core sample slider
On the history page each version is a stone band sized by its change, and the Core sample slider moves by drag and by Up, Down, Home and End with the published value text, lifting the band and showing that version's preview after the rest delay.

Version compare
Enter pins the marker's version as A, the marker's version is B, the Compare region shows the published line diff and counts, and the ?a=v<n>&b=v<m> address restores the same comparison on reload.

Restore a version
Restore appends the next version with the same bytes and sha256 as the restored one, records restored_from, never rewrites or removes a version, and lands the author in the editor on the new head.

Find the version that worked
An author opens history, walks Core sample by keyboard, compares an old version with the head, restores it and lands in the editor with the restored code running in the preview.

Fork a pen
A verified viewer forks a pen they can see, lands in the fork's editor with the fork credit, and the source author's open page shows the new fork count without a reload.

Fork notice email
Forking someone else's public pen sends that author exactly one fork notice, never to the forker and never for an unlisted or private source, and a repeated fork press makes one fork and one email.

Fork lineage and counts
A fork's version 1 has the source head's exact bytes and records the source pen and version, the source's fork count always equals its existing forks, and a fork whose source is gone or hidden shows the published credit instead of a link.

Delete a pen
Deleting a pen removes it, its versions, snapshot objects, likes and collection entries everywhere, its routes answer not found, and its forks remain.

Saves confirmed by storage
A version number appears only after its snapshot is confirmed in storage with a matching hash, numbers per pen are gapless and never reused, and a retried save with the same Idempotency-Key returns the first result.

Version conflict
A save based on an older version is refused with the head number, the editor shows the conflict alert with focus inside it and the edits kept, and its two choices save the edits as the next version or load the latest.

Local draft
While the editor has unsaved edits it keeps a draft in this browser at the configured interval and offers it back after a reload until it is restored, discarded or saved.

Likes
The Like toggle adds or removes exactly one stored like, repeating it is a no-op, and the like count shown always equals the stored likes.

Live updates
Like counts, fork counts and verification state reach every open page within the live-update limit in Business rules without a reload, and changed counts are announced politely.

Collections and tags
An author makes collections, adds pens, reorders them by keyboard with an announced position, and tags pens under the published tag rules, and collection order survives a reload.

Search
Search finds public pens by text and tag: filters, announces the published result count, and always shows the results of the latest query even when an earlier query answers later.

Visibility
The owner moves a pen between private, unlisted and public, and search, the embed route and other people's views follow each change together.

Share sheet
The Share dialog lets the author pick the starting tab with the arrow keys, shows the exact embed link, keeps Tab inside itself, closes with Escape and returns focus to Share.

Embed page
/embed/<pen id> shows the head version read-only, opens on the tab named in tab, switches tabs from the keyboard, reruns the preview, and works without signing in.

Private means not found
For everyone but its owner, a private pen and its versions, renders, embed, fork, like and export answer exactly the same not-found response as a pen that never existed.

Sandboxed preview
Pen code runs only in an iframe sandboxed with scripts but without same-origin, loaded from the app's preview route with the published content policy, so it never reaches the viewer's cookies, storage or page.

Console message gate
The console accepts a message only from the current render's frame carrying that render's nonce, so forged or stale messages show nothing.

Storage outage
When storage is unreachable the health check says so, saving, restoring and exporting show the published outage copy, no version row or number appears, the edits stay, and saving works again without a restart once storage returns.

Export
Export downloads a zip of the head version whose files equal its stored bytes, and a failed export keeps focus on the Export button and shows the published copy.
/app/run.json exists with string install, build and serve and "_schema":"run-manifest-v1", and the app serves only through it.
THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md at /app lists every shipped package (the production dependency tree from npm ls --omit=dev --all --json) plus every shelf library and font, each with its licence.
Every shipped package, shelf library and font uses MIT, ISC, BSD-2-Clause, BSD-3-Clause, Apache-2.0, 0BSD or OFL-1.1.
The only datastores are the provided Postgres database and MinIO bucket; no SQLite, embedded key-value store, extra search engine or file used as a database.
At runtime the app loads no script, style, font or image from any outside host.
The provided service definitions and environment files stay unedited.
Server and client source is TypeScript, with no hand-written .js source files except build or tool configuration.
